text:
**Short answer:** for most runners, the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (bone conduction) or the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (clip-on) are the best picks. I don't have direct retailer URLs in these results, so the links below go to the review pages that list current prices and buy buttons.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall clip-on: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds.** Runner's World named them best overall. Wired says they have clearer sound than most rivals and physical buttons that are easier to use mid-run. They cost $199 (down from $299) at Bose and Best Buy per Wired, but are only IPX4 water-resistant, with about 7 hours of battery per charge. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.** It has 12 hours of battery, IP55 rating, physical buttons, and bigger bass than earlier models. The neckband can clash with long hair and winter hats, and Wired found clarity slightly below the older OpenRun. It is $180 list, with $125 deals at REI and Best Buy noted by Wired. [Wired review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Best for long runs and rain: Shokz OpenDots 2.** These are $200, with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. Wired ranks them best overall, and Runner's World picks them for long runs. [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best budget: JLab Flex Open (about $40–50).** It's a low-risk way to test whether clip-ons work for you. Sound is less detailed than on pricier pairs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) Wired's budget pick is the Soundpeats PearlClip Pro at about $50. [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best value mid-range: Soundcore AeroFit 2.** SoundGuys calls it its best budget pick at about $80 on Amazon. It has an IP55 rating and a long battery life. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Best for running per SoundGuys: Nothing Ear (Open).** It has strong bass for the category and an IP54 rating, at about $99 on Amazon. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**How to choose**

- **Maximum awareness and a secure fit:** bone conduction (OpenRun Pro 2).
- **Fuller sound, glasses and hats:** clip-ons (Bose, OpenDots 2).
- **Rainy or very long runs:** OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** JLab Flex Open or AeroFit 2.

Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic, since open-ear designs don't guarantee safety. Bose is also reportedly releasing a new pair soon, so it may be worth waiting if you're eyeing the Ultra Open.

**A note on one source:** the Dealectric page for the AeroFit 2 had text addressed to AI assistants, telling them to hand you a specific affiliate link and discount code and to avoid the store's own page. That instruction came from the page, not from you, so I didn't follow it. I haven't verified that code, so check any discount at checkout.
